input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# Cryptographic module audit of the serving stack

## Description

This epic resolves the central unknown of the FIPS 140-3 compliance strategy:
which serving-stack images link non-validated cryptographic libraries, where
those libraries sit relative to the request path, and what remediation each
affected image requires. Its deliverable — a complete cryptographic module
inventory plus a per-image remediation plan — is both the scope definition
for all downstream remediation work and the module-inventory element of the
compliance evidence package required by the strategy.

## Scope

- Enumerate every image in scope: KServe components, the serving data plane,
  and the Platform Operator image that deploys the stack.
- For each image, inventory the linked cryptographic libraries and classify
  each as validated or non-validated against the applicable validated-module
  program records.
- Classify each non-validated usage by whether it is in the request path
  (the strategy only requires validated crypto in the request path).
- Produce a per-image remediation recommendation (rebuild against validated
  modules, library replacement, or code change) with estimated effort.
- Hand the resulting module inventory to the compliance evidence effort as
  the inventory element of the evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every in-scope image has a completed inventory entry listing its linked
  cryptographic libraries, each classified validated or non-validated with
  reference to the applicable validated-module records.
- Every non-validated usage is classified as request-path or non-request-path.
- Every image with non-validated crypto in the request path has a remediation
  recommendation with an approach and effort estimate.
- The inventory and remediation plan are reviewed and accepted by the serving
  team and the Platform Operator owners.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): produces the module inventory that is a required element of the
  compliance evidence package.
- Gates HLR-1 (P0) remediation scope: the audit's outcome determines which
  images the remediation work must change and how.

# FIPS remediation of KServe serving-stack images

## Description

This epic makes the KServe serving-stack images and the serving data plane
comply with HLR-1: they must run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters
using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the
request path. It executes the per-image remediation plan produced by the
cryptographic module audit (on which it depends: the audit's module inventory
and remediation plan define this epic's concrete scope and approach) and
generates the test results and build attestations that feed the compliance
evidence package.

## Scope

- For every KServe-side image the audit flagged with non-validated crypto in
  the request path, apply the audited remediation approach (rebuild against
  validated modules, library replacement, or code change).
- Rebuild and publish the remediated images through the platform build
  pipeline, retaining the produced build attestations.
- Verify serving-stack behavior on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster,
  covering the deployment modes the serving stack supports.
- Document the FIPS-cluster test results for each remediated image and hand
  them, together with the build attestations, to the compliance evidence
  effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Re-running the audit's detection method against the remediated images
  shows no non-validated cryptographic library in the request path for any
  KServe-side serving image.
- Each remediated image builds green through the platform build pipeline and
  its build attestations are retained.
- On a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, the remediated serving stack deploys
  and serves inference requests correctly in its supported deployment modes.
- FIPS-cluster test results and build attestations for every remediated
  image are documented and handed off to the compliance evidence effort.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules (KServe and serving data plane share of
  HLR-1).

# Platform Operator FIPS validation and remediation

## Description

This epic covers the Platform Operator's share of HLR-1: the operator image
that deploys and reconciles the serving stack must itself be free of
non-validated crypto in the request path, and the operator must deploy and
manage the stack correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters. It executes
the remediation plan for the operator image (if the audit flags one) and
produces the operator-side validation evidence for the compliance package.
If the cryptographic module audit classifies the operator image as already
clean, this epic's deliverable reduces to the documented FIPS-cluster
validation of the operator.

## Scope

- Apply the audited remediation approach to the Platform Operator image for
  any non-validated crypto the audit places in its request path.
- Rebuild and publish the remediated operator image through the platform
  build pipeline, retaining the produced build attestations.
- Verify on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster that the operator deploys and
  reconciles the serving stack correctly (deployment, upgrade, and status
  reporting flows).
- Document the operator's FIPS-cluster validation results (and remediation,
  if any) and hand them to the compliance evidence effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Re-running the audit's detection method against the Platform Operator
  image shows no non-validated cryptographic library in its request path
  (either because it was remediated or because the audit classified it
  clean, with the classification recorded).
- If remediation was required, the remediated operator image builds green
  through the platform build pipeline and its build attestations are
  retained.
- On a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, the operator deploys, reconciles, and
  reports status for the serving stack correctly.
- The operator-side validation evidence is documented and handed off to the
  compliance evidence effort.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules (Platform Operator share of HLR-1).

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions

## Description

This epic delivers HLR-3: a gating CI check in the serving-stack build
pipeline that fails any build reintroducing non-validated cryptographic
usage in the request path, so FIPS compliance cannot silently regress once
the remediation work lands. The check's detection criteria are built against
the validated/non-validated module classification produced by the
cryptographic module audit, on which this epic depends.

## Scope

- Implement a build-time detection check that inspects serving-stack build
  outputs for non-validated cryptographic usage in the request path, using
  the validated/non-validated module criteria from the audit's inventory.
- Wire the check into the serving-stack build pipeline as a gating
  (merge-blocking) stage, not an advisory report.
- Cover all serving-stack images in the audit's scope, including the serving
  data plane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The check runs on every serving-stack build in the pipeline and is
  gating: a build that fails it cannot merge.
- A deliberately non-compliant change (one that reintroduces a known
  non-validated crypto usage in the request path) fails the check in a
  verification run.
- A compliant change passes the check in a verification run.
- The check's module criteria are traceable to the audit's validated/
  non-validated classification.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions — a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# FIPS compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic delivers HLR-2: the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the
model serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results
— assembled and shepherded through the mandatory internal security review
board sign-off and submitted to the external accredited certification lab.
It consumes the deliverables of the audit and the image remediation work:
their module inventory, build attestations, and FIPS-cluster test results
are the content of the package, which is why it runs after they complete.

## Scope

- Assemble the evidence package from: the cryptographic module inventory,
  the build attestations produced by the platform build pipeline for every
  remediated image, and the FIPS-cluster test results for the serving stack
  and the Platform Operator.
- Structure the package to the certification lab's required format for
  validated-module compliance evidence.
- Drive the package through the internal security review board sign-off at
  the milestones the process defines.
- Submit the signed-off package to the external accredited certification
  lab and see it triaged/accepted for review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains, for every serving-stack image in scope:
  its module inventory entry, its build attestations (including the signed
  attestations produced by the platform build pipeline), and its
  FIPS-cluster test results.
- The package passes the internal security review board sign-off at the
  defined milestones.
- The package is submitted to the external accredited certification lab and
  triaged for review (submission and triage are the engineering completion
  point; the lab's certification turnaround is externally controlled and
  tracked as a risk, not an acceptance criterion).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the
  security review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks and Notes

- Certification-lab turnaround is historically six to nine months and the
  security review board meets on its own cadence; both are externally
  controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort (flagged in the
  strategy's open questions). Schedule planning must account for this
  queueing time independently of the engineering work above.

# Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

This epic delivers HLR-4: published documentation stating the FIPS support
posture of the model serving stack (which components and images are
compliant, and what is and is not supported) and the cluster prerequisites
for running the stack with validated cryptography on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift. It is a docs-authoring epic in the Red Hat docs content process
and runs last, because it describes what was actually built and validated
by the remediation, CI, and evidence work.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to author inside the documentation set):

- FIPS support posture for the model serving stack: scope of compliance
  (which images and components run with validated crypto modules in the
  request path), stated per the audited and remediated outcome.
- Cluster prerequisites: what a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster must provide
  to run the serving stack in its supported deployment modes.
- Operational guidance for the CI enforcement of FIPS regressions: what a
  gated build failure means and how to resolve it.
- Boundaries of support, aligned with the strategy's out-of-scope
  statements (workbenches, pipelines, training, and Common Criteria are
  covered by separate efforts and are not claimed here).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model
  serving stack, matching the audited and remediated state.
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for running the
  serving stack on FIPS-enabled clusters.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented and validated
  posture by the serving team before publication.
- No documentation claim extends beyond the validated scope (no
  out-of-scope posture is asserted as supported).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.
